title: The picture the game draws for a control
summary: TCG Card Shop Simulator does not describe a control in words: an interactable carries lists of the pictures to draw, and the game ships its own artwork for a mouse click, a mouse hold and the keys on a keyboard.
body: A prompt is drawn rather than written. An object you can interact with carries a list of input displays, which is why the game can put the right picture next to an action instead of describing it.
Controllers get their own list. There is a second list for displays that only appear when a pad is in use, so the same action does not have to show a keyboard and a pad at once.
The mouse is drawn as a picture. The game ships an image of a left mouse click and a separate one for holding the button down, which is why a prompt can tell a press apart from a hold at a glance.
Keys are drawn as pictures too, one per key. The game ships a plain key picture and named ones for the keys it needs, which is how a binding can be shown without spelling out a name.
Named keys cover the ones the game leans on. There are key pictures for control, tab and shift, so a combination can be drawn as two pictures side by side rather than as a word.
The screen has a cursor of its own. There is a part of the game whose job is to set the cursor, so the pointer can change with what is under it.
Playing a card has buttons of its own. There is a group of buttons kept for playing a card, which is why the card game can put its own controls on screen rather than reusing the shop's.
What this entry does not tell you: how many controls the game can show, which keys have pictures, or how a prompt is laid out. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: An interactable carries a list of input displays, with a second list for controller-only displays.
The game ships a picture of a left mouse click and another for holding the button.
It ships a plain key picture as well as named key pictures.
Named key pictures cover control, tab and shift.
Part of the game is there to set the cursor.
Playing a card has a group of buttons of its own.
The pad pictures are shipped one per control, covering the four face buttons, the d-pad directions, the triggers and the stick clicks.
facts.evidence: asset names: XBox_A_Fontstyle, XBox_B_Fontstyle, XBox_X_Fontstyle, XBox_Y_Fontstyle, XBox_Dpad_Right_Fontstyle, XBox_LT_Fontstyle

facts.claim: A light tap on a control has a sound of its own, with a pad version beside it.
